newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury delays sale of indexed notes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury delays sale of indexed notes.

text.p: The Treasury Department's first 10-year note designed to protect investors against inflation, expected to be sold early in January, will be unveiled later, a senior Treasury official said on Monday.

"There's going to be a slight delay in the first auction of indexed notes," Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson said. He declined to specify exactly why or for how long it will be delayed.

"We haven't finalised the terms and conditions," Anderson told reporters. "We recognise that market participants will need some time to review the final terms and conditions, therefore there's got to be a slight delay."
The specific wording of a 60-to-70-page circular setting out terms and conditions of the securities sales, which will be published in the Federal Register, was being worked out, Anderson said.

The first auction of the new securities, which Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin originally announced last May, had been expected to occur sometime during the first two weeks of January for settlement -- or payment by investors -- on Jan. 15.
Anderson could not say when the first sale actually will take place but said the delay would not be lengthy.
"We don't have a schedule yet," he said. "But we expect (the delay) to be slight."

Securities dealers had suggested the Treasury delay the auction. Dealers need to set up computer systems to handle the accounting for the new security and some mutual funds reportedly are preparing to set up funds that are geared to the new type of security.

Rubin has suggested the inflation-protected securities would be a good investment vehicle for individuals saving for retirement or for long-term purposes like paying for education costs. They offer absolute security since the government is the debtor and protect against inflation eating away the value of principle.
Though the first issue will be a 10-year note, Treasury has indicated it likely will add other maturities of inflation-protected securities if demand is as strong as it anticipates.
